prompt:
Create a production sprite atlas for a children's English vocabulary game. One square canvas divided mathematically into exactly 3 columns and 3 rows of equal square cells, nine illustrations total. Cell boundaries must be exactly at 1/3 and 2/3 of the canvas in both axes. Follow this exact placement:
Row 1, left to right: one cat; one dog; one rabbit.
Row 2, left to right: one bear; one panda; one monkey.
Row 3, left to right: one pig; one cow; one elephant.
Style: warm hand-painted children's picture-book gouache, rounded clear silhouettes, natural colors, subtle paper texture, soft upper-left lighting, gentle grounded shadows. Uniform warm ivory background #faf7ef across the entire canvas. Each subject is fully contained inside its own cell and centered, occupies around 65-70% of that cell, with at least 12% internal padding on every side. Equal visual scale. No drawn grid lines, no outer border, no additional gutters that change the equal cell geometry; the internal blank padding naturally separates the cells. Each cell contains only its specified subject, fully visible and recognizable at 100 pixels. No text, letters, numerals, labels, watermarks, extra objects, scenery, plates, or people. Never duplicate, swap, omit or merge a subject. Food and objects have no faces. All nine illustrations look painted by the same children's book illustrator.
